title: Notification circuit compiler for incident workflows
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Incidents today generate noisy, monolithic PagerDuty pages and long Slack threads that lack targeted remediation context. On-call engineers spend time triaging unrelated signals and hunting for the right runbook sections and traces. We need an automated, auditable way to compile a tailored "notification circuit" for each triggered incident that bundles: the filtered trace snippets, prioritized metrics slices, a curated runbook fragment, interactive Slack actions (rollback/run diagnostics), and a PD incident payload with response play links.

Goal: Build a service that compiles contextual incident delivery bundles (notification circuits) by synthesizing telemetry, runbook fragments, and responder routing policy. Deliverables: 1) a compiler service that accepts a telemetry signature and returns a PD + Slack bundle, 2) hooks to trace ingestion to produce compact snippets, 3) runbook fragment storage and versioning integration, 4) safety and opt-out controls for sensitive payloads.

Design highlights and trade-offs:
- Compiler approach: We chose a rule-based pipeline with pluggable heuristics (span-weighted selectors, metric anomaly scorers) rather than an early ML model. Trade-off: faster rollout and deterministic audits vs. lower initial signal synthesis quality.
- Runbook fragments: store as small, tagged sections (idempotent snippets) rather than full runbooks to reduce noise and make updates atomic. We'll link fragments back to Confluence/Drive for full context.
- Slack interactivity: provision ephemeral action tokens (1-hour lifetime) and only surface command templates (no broad run-anything buttons) to reduce blast radius.
- PagerDuty payloads: use severity-weighted responder lists and include a compact evidence package (trace ids, top-5 spans, key metric deltas). Payload size capped to 150KB; fall back to a hosted evidence bundle if larger.
- Privacy/security: redact PII from traces via the existing telemetry redaction library and require security review for the compiler before GA.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype compiler service and selector heuristics (2 sprints): implement span scorer, metrics delta extractor, fragment assembler, and a dry-run PD + Slack payload generator.
2) Integrate with trace hook: add a lightweight post-processor to the trace ingestion pipeline to compute snippet candidates and store them in the evidence artifact store.
3) Runbook fragment store: extend the runbook service to support fragmenting, version tags, and a small REST API for resolution.
4) Connect to PD/Slack adapters: implement a preview mode that opens a private Slack DM to the owner and a PD test incident for verification.
5) Canary rollout to internal SRE and one product team, gather feedback, iterate.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Mean time to first meaningful action (MTFA) reduction by 20% for canary teams.
- Reduction in Slack messages in incident threads by 30% (measured by message count per incident).
- Evidence bundle recall: on sampled incidents, the compiler must include the correct trace span in the top-3 candidates 90% of the time.
- No increase in false P0 escalations (tracked via PD manual downgrades).

Backward compatibility and opt-outs:
- Default behavior is opt-in per-service. Existing PD/Slack integrations remain unchanged until a team flips the compiler flag.
- Provide a route that returns the compiled bundle as JSON for audit and debugging.

Security and compliance:
- Marked security_review_required: true. Security review checklist: token scope review, ephemeral token expiry, evidence bundle storage encryption (KMS), audit logging for bundle generation and access.
- Data retention: evidence artifacts retained for 90 days by default, configurable per-org.

Testing plan and rollout:
- Unit tests for each selector and fragment resolver.
- Integration tests: end-to-end dry-run creating a PD test incident and Slack DM.
- Load test the compiler at 200 incidents/min to validate latency targets (95p < 1200ms for compilation).
- Canary for 3 weeks with internal SRE, measure MTFA, iterate on heuristics.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Which query language to use for fragment tagging? (Confluence labels vs. small YAML tags). Action: PM and Docs to pick by 2026-02-18.
- Evidence bundle storage location: use existing telemetry S3 bucket or new encrypted evidence store? Action: infra to advise by 2026-02-20.

Links and artifacts: design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/notification-circuit-compiler (draft), prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/4112, fragment API spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Fragment+API (WIP).
